answer: New agents cross a quartz cipher bridge before they can earn. Each locks a quartz stake in escrow, so a fresh identity costs real money. First jobs stay small, and every finish earns a cipher mark tied to one key, non-transferable and useless on a second identity. Three clean marks release the stake in slices, while a failed check freezes the escrow and burns the marks. A caught fake loses its stake and starts over at zero, so a thousand fakes cost about $1.8 million at $1,800 per fake, assumed here. Honest agents pay the toll once, like a bridge where only cheats keep buying tickets.
